newsitem.title: USA: U.S. ACCOUNTANTS BACK FASB'S DERIVATIVE PROPOSALS.
newsitem.headline: U.S. ACCOUNTANTS BACK FASB'S DERIVATIVE PROPOSALS.

text.p: U.S. accountants are backing Financial Accounting Standards Board derivative accounting proposals, stating that investor protection, not politics, should guide financial reporting in this complex area.

The American Institute of Certified Public Accountants issued a statement in support of FASB's role as primary accounting standards setter stating: "The issue of derivatives has involved much controversy and debate, and has been on the agenda of a great number of FASB meeings."

As a result of this open deliberative process, the statement continues, "the diverse viewponts have been throughly discussed...(and) FASB has been responsive, (making) alterations to its original draft proposals in order to take into account the valid concerns of different parties."

The statement from the national professional organization of CPAs follows release of Federal Reserve Board Chairman Alan Greenspan's July 31 letter to FASB urging the board to slow down and allow more time for industry input, and recommending it consider a different proposal altogether.

Greenspan's comments came after a group of top executives from major U.S. corporations blasted FASB for moving quickly to finalize the rules, claiming they would weaken a company's ability to manage risk.
The accountants' group, which has been on the side of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on this issue, concluded:

"The enormous growth in the quantity and complexity of financial transactions involving derivatives has made accounting properly for derivatives critical for our financial reporting system. The technical accounting issues involved are extremely complex -- too complex to be determined according to purely political pressures. The AICPA believes it is investor protection that is at stake, and it is investor protection that must guide decisions in this difficult and complex area -- not politics."
